blockers: Requires legislation; the H-2A program has no statutory numerical cap and the H-2B cap is set by statute and adjusted by supplemental authority.
The Mandate itself records that some conservatives favor the programs, and agricultural and seasonal employers rely on them.
confidence_reason: The FY2026 H-2B supplemental visa rule was confirmed in the Federal Register and runs opposite to the Mandate's call for a cap; the H-2A wage rule was not re-read, and congressional bills were not searched, though a cap would require legislation that no source indicates has advanced.

court_status.basis: derived from the latest court event in the timeline

durability.why: The wage-rate and supplemental-visa actions are administrative and reversible; any cap would need a statute to be durable.

est_completion.basis: Inference: the recommendation needs an act of Congress and the administration's measured actions so far expanded or adjusted the programs rather than limiting them.

proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress immediately cap the H-2A agricultural visa program at current levels and phase it down over 10 to 20 years (alongside an industry consortium to fund farm automation), and cap and phase out the H-2B seasonal nonagricultural program over no more than 10 years. It records alternative conservative views that favor keeping both programs.
remaining: Congress would need to enact a cap and a phase-down schedule for H-2A and H-2B; no such bill was searched for or found.
A farm-automation industry consortium with matching federal funds, as the Mandate recommends (no action found).

review.mandate_note: Pages 611 to 612 recommend that Congress immediately cap H-2A at current levels and phase it down over 10 to 20 years with an industry automation consortium, and cap and phase out H-2B within 10 years, and record Alternative View paragraphs from conservatives who favor both programs; the paraphrase, including the alternative views, and pages match.

source_checks.note: Joint DHS and DOL temporary final rule at 91 FR 5040 (2026-02-03), applying 2026-01-30 through 2026-09-30, makes up to 64,716 supplemental H-2B visas available for FY2026 in three allocations, citing employers' inability to find U.S. workers and strong demand; this is an expansion, opposite to the Mandate's cap.

significance.rationale: Capping and phasing out H-2A and H-2B would end two temporary worker programs relied on by agriculture and seasonal employers.

status_summary: No cap or phase-down was found. DOL issued an interim final rule on 2025-10-02 changing how H-2A wage rates are set (using BLS data in place of the discontinued USDA farm labor survey), citing labor shortage and food-supply concerns. On 2026-02-03 DHS and DOL published a temporary final rule making up to 64,716 supplemental H-2B visas available for FY2026 above the statutory limit. Both actions keep or expand the programs, which runs opposite to the Mandate's recommendation to cap and reduce them; the Mandate also records alternative conservative views favoring the programs.

timeline.event: A federal court in Louisiana enters final judgment vacating DOL's 2023 H-2A wage-rate rule (Teche Vermilion Sugar Cane Growers v. Su), returning the program to the 2010 methodology, according to DOL's later rule.

DOL publishes an interim final rule, effective immediately, setting H-2A adverse effect wage rates for non-range occupations from BLS wage data by skill level instead of USDA survey data. DOL cites a claimed labor shortage tied to reduced illegal immigration and the end of the USDA survey; 887 comments were received by 2025-12-01. DOL reports H-2A worker requests rose from about 286,900 (FY2020) to about 391,600 (FY2024).

A Federal Register rule from DOL (listed with the Department's rules) exercises time-limited authority to increase the FY2026 numerical limitation for the H-2B program. The number of added visas was not read in this research.

title: Cap and phase down the H-2A and H-2B temporary worker visa programs
uncertainties: The H-2B rule page could not be read (fetch rate limit), so the number of added visas, the issuing agencies and the stated reasons are unverified; only its title and date come from the Federal Register listing. The effect of the H-2A wage change on wage levels was not verified and no characterization is made. Congressional bills to cap H-2A or H-2B were not searched. The DOL agenda lists an H-2B wage-survey final rule projected for 2026-04, whose issuance was not checked. 'Diverged' reflects that the H-2B limit was raised, which is the opposite of the Mandate's cap; the H-2A action is a different design and not a direct reversal.
